articles.title: Ethanol policy shift: India bars sugar-based feedstocks, reduces maize procurement price
articles.description: India has made a major change to its ethanol procurement strategy, excluding key sugar-based feedstocks and reducing maize incentives. Here's what the move means for the E20 petrol programme.

articles.title: India bars sugar-based ethanol in 2026-27 tender, cuts maize incentive
articles.description: New Delhi: State-run oil marketing companies have barred ethanol made from sugarcane juice, sugar syrup and B-heavy molasses from their latest procurement tender for the 2026-27 supply year for blending in petrol, as the government seeks to protect domestic sugar supplies while sustaining its nationwide petrol-blending programme. articles.title: Kerala eyes joint drug tenders to cut costs, plug supply gaps
articles.description: Kerala plans to partner with other states for joint medicine procurement to reduce costs, prevent shortages, and revise restrictive tender conditions that currently deter smaller pharmaceutical manufacturers from bidding for government hospital contracts.

articles.title: ₹200 Crore School Furniture Procurement Row In Madhya Pradesh! RSK's ₹44.35 Crore Direct Orders Raise Questions
articles.description: Madhya Pradesh's Rajya Shiksha Kendra faces scrutiny over ₹44.35 crore furniture orders issued to three firms under an existing MPLUN tender. The ₹200 crore procurement arrangement has raised questions about tender compliance and discrepancies in purchase documents. Meanwhile, the finance controller has reportedly withheld payments despite directions from senior officials.

articles.title: Delhi court rejects bail pleas of former DGHS Vatsala Aggarwal, Vinod Kumar Ranga
articles.description: The Rouse Avenue Court on Saturday rejected the bail applications of former Director General of Health Services DGHS Dr Vatsala Aggarwal and Dr Vinod Kumar Ranga in an alleged Rs 700-crore corruption case involving the procurement of medical goods at higher prices citing the gravity of the offences and the need for further investigation Their continued custody is necessary in order to ensure fair and unhindered investigation as there is apprehension that they may influence the investigation the court said
